criteria.note: windowed_spend is horizon-scoped (4h+60s spend over a 4h window = 0); measure_per_worker_rate arithmetic exact (8000/14400/4); no live remaining-token count queried.

The min (tighter window) wins in BOTH directions (tight session -> 3; default -> weekly 8 not session 13); bootstrap (rate 0 and -5) -> max_workers; at-least-one when a worker outpaces a window (n=1 not 0); cap holds; never negative or nonsense.
Each window independently forces 0 when over budget (a weekly-only over-budget forces 0 with the session clear); limit cooldown boundary correct (now==cooldown runs, future backs off).

resume_at verified at resume +/- epsilon across one-big-spend, five-small (JUST enough oldest age out), multi-window (the MAX), oversized-single, and under-budget (returns now) cases; NEVER points at a strictly-over-budget time; computes only, no sleep/spawn/socket (imports importlib.util + pathlib only).

now_epoch a parameter everywhere, reads no wall clock; gate GREEN, selftest 1047; mutation min->max reddens the tighter-window assertion, neutralizing the spent-out return 0 reddens the backs-off assertion.

findings.text: Independent adversarial review, PASS, 0 blocking. The control law and resume_at are correct: desired_workers paces to the tighter window's target rate with at-least-one-while-budget-remains and bootstrap-to-max, backs off to 0 on a spent-out window or a limit cooldown, and resume_at is verified never to point at a strictly-over-budget time. Reproductions run against the real governor.py with a deterministic base time; both mutation teeth (min->max, ignore-backoff) confirmed red.

Four accepted non-blocking notes, all benign: (1) resume_at is the infimum - at the exact returned instant windowed_spend == budget under the inclusive trailing filter, so desired_workers still returns 0 there and the pool is clear only at +epsilon; safe because the launcher re-checks desired_workers on wake (Y7 must and does re-gate). (2) Future-dated events are counted (no upper time bound), conservative and safe for clock-skew. (3) A for/else branch in resume_at is dead but computes the identical value (harmless). (4) int(tokens) is unguarded, matching existing metrics.py behavior for system-produced integer spend. None affect correctness of the pacing or resume timing.

summary: Y6 (WARP-0706, the token pacing governor) is correct and honest. Independent adversarial review pass_with_notes, 0 blocking; gate GREEN (selftest 1047). It measures burn from the event stream within rolling windows (never querying a live remaining count, which Claude Code does not expose) and paces the active worker count to the tighter window's target rate - at least one worker while budget remains so the budget is used, none while a window's budget is spent in its horizon or during a limit cooldown - and resume_at computes when a backed-off pool may resume, verified never to point at a strictly-over-budget time. It is a pure stdlib control law with now_epoch as a parameter (deterministic) that spawns no process and sleeps nothing; the opt-in in-session resume waiter is deferred to the launcher (Y7), never a detached process. proof_digest via validate.py.
